page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-192 is a high-capacity virtual machine instance belonging to the c4d server family. It features 192 dedicated vCPUs built on the x86_64 CPU architecture. The instance is equipped with 1512.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 7.88 GB of RAM per core. This configuration does not include any local storage or bundled GPUs, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The resource allocation profile of this instance leans heavily toward memory-intensive operations, offering a high density of RAM relative to its 192 dedicated vCPUs. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the lack of integrated local storage and GPU hardware means that users only pay for raw compute and memory capacity, avoiding the overhead of unneeded specialized hardware. However, workloads requiring fast local scratch space or hardware acceleration will face tradeoffs, as they must rely on network-attached storage or separate GPU-enabled instances. This server is suited for large-scale databases, in-memory analytics, enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, and memory-heavy data processing pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-192 is an x86_64 architecture server within the c4d family, configured with 192 dedicated vCPUs and 1512.0 GB of RAM. This configuration provides a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of approximately 7.88 GB per core, positioning it for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, which simplifies the hardware profile and focuses cost efficiency on compute and memory density. Without local NVMe drives or hardware accelerators, the instance requires network-attached storage for persistent data. It is suited for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise applications, and heavy data processing tasks that require substantial memory capacity alongside a high count of dedicated virtual processors.
